answer: Each new identity locks 60 credits in a mesa vault, sealed by a ferrous seal binding its key to that entry. A mesa auditor must also lock a bond to verify it: 90 credits for a first verification in an epoch, 180 for a second, at most two per auditor per epoch. A gale audit recomputes the seal and entry from the mesa board; a mismatch burns both bonds. The 1000th fake identity costs 240, and 1,000 fakes lock 195,000 credits total, against 60 for one honest identity. A rented-auditor ring fails because auditors keep doubling bonds while gale audits burn bonds of auditors who verified a fake.
